# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python)

## 1. Overall Structure, Language, Framework

**Language/stack:** Python 3.9, Flask 1.1.2 web service (rule/regex-based, heavy use of pandas `np.select` condition tables; fuzzywuzzy/Levenshtein for name matching; scipy/sklearn clustering for salary detection). Deployed via gunicorn on port 9898 (see `/app/Dockerfile`).

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # package deps (Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, sklearn...)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory, request timing logging
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP routes / orchestration pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 per-bank categorizers (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # cross-bank enrichment (purpose, clean names, salary, PFM...)
```

**Flow (`Controller.py`):** `POST /categorizeTransaction` receives `{bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, transactions[]}` → per-bank `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` (assigns `transactionCategory` + extracts `partyName`) → `purpose()` (assigns `transactionSubcategory`) → `clean_names()` (canonical payee names) → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` (SAVING only) → optional PFM categorization + simple description. There is also `POST /recurrentTransactions`.

## 2. Files Responsible for Categorization/Enrichment

### Category assignment (transactionCategory) + payee extraction per bank
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` — 35 files (`HDFC.py`, `SBI.py`, `ICICI.py`, `Axis.py`, `Kotak.py`, `BOB.py`, `PNB.py`, `YES.py`, `Indusind.py`, etc.). Each `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` is a big ordered regex condition table over `description` assigning `transactionCategory` values such as `UPI`, `IMPS`, `NEFT`, `RTGS`, `TPT`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `IMPS_REVERSAL`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `NEFT_RETURN`, `SALARY`, `REFUND`, `CASH_DEPOSIT`, charges/penalties, etc. The **same files also extract the raw counterparty** into `partyName` (e.g., `HDFC.py` lines ~108–230) using splitter helpers.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` — routing + per-bank pipeline orchestration (one near-identical block per bank).

### Sub-tag / sub-category assignment (transactionSubcategory)
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — `purpose(transactions, accountType)`; assigns subcategories: SALARY, SALARY_DISBURSED, REIMBURSEMENT, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, INVESTMENT, CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, FUEL, TRAVEL, EDUCATION, FOOD, E_COMMERCE, RENT, etc.; also tags `merchantType` (NBFC, HFC, Instant Loan, Vehicle Loan...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` — same idea for CREDIT_CARD accounts (`card_purpose`).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` — `pfm_categorization()`: maps to personal-finance-management categories when `isPFMEnabled`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` — `simple_description()`: human-readable description for a whitelist of categories.

### Payee/counterparty name cleaning
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (1971 lines) — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`: canonicalizes `partyName` to merchant names ("TataSky DTH", "Adani Electricity", ...) via thousands of regex rules.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` (927 lines) — same for credit-card transactions (`card_clean_names`).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` — helpers: `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_*` description splitters, `fuzzy_match`, `py_extract`.

### Transfer / cheque / salary / reversal / bounce detection
- **Transfer (self/internal):** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` — `internal_payment()`: fuzzy-matches account-holder name against `partyName` for categories like NEFT/IMPS/RTGS/UPI/CHEQUE_* to set subcategory `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` and `isInternalPayment` flag; excludes `INWARD_BOUNCE`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `REVERSAL`.
- **Salary:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` — `salary_detection()`: statistical approach; clusters party names (Levenshtein distance + hierarchical `cut_tree`), filters credits > 2999, checks monthly recurrence to tag SALARY. Rule-based salary regexes also in `Purpose.py` (SALARY, SAL_IMPS, NOT_SAL patterns).
- **Cheque / reversal / bounce (rule level):** detected inside each `BankScripts/*.py` regex table (e.g., `HDFC.py` lines 21–30, 50, 69–75: `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`, `REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `IMPS_REVERSAL`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `NEFT_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`). Bounce enums: `INWARD_BOUNCE`/`OUTWARD_BOUNCE`/`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`.

### Shared regex/enum definitions
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — shared regex constants (SALARY, LOAN, INSURANCE, INVEST, ...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` — bank-specific regex constants (BANK_VER, BANK_CHARGES_HDFC, ...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` — enum-to-display-name mappings for all category/subcategory labels (reference only; the scripts use string literals).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py` — `recurrent_transactions()`: flags recurring transactions (separate endpoint).

## 3. Test Files

**None.** There are no test files, `tests/` directories, `conftest.py`, pytest/unittest imports, `test_*` functions, or CI configs anywhere in the repo (searched for `pytest|unittest|def test_`, `test*` globs, tox/Makefile/README — nothing found). The only test-adjacent artifact is a commented-out dendrogram plot "For testing purpose only" inside `SalaryDetection.py`.

## 4. How to Run Tests

There is no test suite or test runner configured, so there is nothing to run. To exercise the code you would run the service manually and hit its HTTP endpoints:

```bash
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or: FLASK_APP=categorizationapp flask run --port 9898
# then POST JSON to /categorizeTransaction or /recurrentTransactions
```

(Or build/run the Docker image per `/app/Dockerfile`.) If tests are desired, they would need to be added from scratch (e.g., pytest against `purpose()`, `clean_names()`, and the `categorize_*_transactions()` functions, which are all pure DataFrame-in/DataFrame-out and easily unit-testable — note some modules import `from categorizationapp import app`, so a Flask app context/import is pulled in).

"""Repro for forum digest: edge rows getting wrong category/sub-tag/payee.

Case 1 (mango_saver a): HDFC credit whose remark is a long all-numeric string
          -> expected CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, currently generic TRANSFER.
Case 2 (mango_saver b): HDFC salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code
          -> expected sub-tag SALARY, currently blank.
Case 3 (rk_ontheroad): ICICI transfer whose narration opens with a direction word
          ("TRFR TO:<name>") -> expected payee, currently empty/wrong.
Case 4 (auditlens): ICICI slash-delimited bill transfer with four fields
          (type/sub-type/numeric-ref/payee) -> expected final-field payee,
          currently the numeric reference.
Case 5 (maintainer): HDFC offsetting credit immediately after matching debit
          -> expected REVERSAL, currently AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE.
"""
import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions

def frame(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df["amount"])
    df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = pd.to_numeric(df["balanceAfterTransaction"])
    return df

failures = []

def check(label, actual, expected):
    ok = actual == expected
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"[{status}] {label}: expected={expected!r} actual={actual!r}")
    if not ok:
        failures.append(label)

# ---- Case 1: HDFC all-numeric remark credit -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT ----
t = frame([{"description": "DEPOSIT TRANSFER BRANCH", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 25000,
            "remark": "0000000000012345", "balanceAfterTransaction": 50000}])
r = categorize_HDFC_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("1 HDFC numeric-remark credit category", r.transactionCategory.iloc[0], "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT")

# ---- Case 2: HDFC bare 6-digit narration salary credit -> sub-tag SALARY ----
t = frame([{"description": "123456", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 55000,
            "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 80000}])
r = categorize_HDFC_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("2 HDFC numeric-narration category (unchanged)", r.transactionCategory.iloc[0], "TRANSFER")
check("2 HDFC numeric-narration salary sub-tag", r.transactionSubcategory.iloc[0], "SALARY")

# ---- Case 3: ICICI narration opening with direction word -> payee name ----
t = frame([{"description": "TRFR TO:JOHN DOE", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 1200,
            "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 4000}])
r = categorize_ICICI_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("3 ICICI TRFR TO: payee", r.partyName.iloc[0], "John Doe")

t = frame([{"description": "TRFR FROM:JANE SMITH", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 1200,
            "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 4000}])
r = categorize_ICICI_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("3 ICICI TRFR FROM: payee", r.partyName.iloc[0], "Jane Smith")

# ---- Case 4: ICICI BIL/INFT four-field reference -> final-field payee ----
t = frame([{"description": "BIL/INFT/026094953716/ANAMICA CHATTERJEE", "type": "DEBIT",
            "amount": 3000, "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 9000}])
r = categorize_ICICI_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("4 ICICI BIL/INFT 4-field payee", r.partyName.iloc[0], "Anamica Chatterjee")

# regression: 5-field BIL/INFT rows keep using the 5th field (rule below it)
t = frame([{"description": "BIL/INFT/026094953716/REMARK X/RAVI KUMAR", "type": "DEBIT",
            "amount": 3000, "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 9000}])
r = categorize_ICICI_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("4r ICICI BIL/INFT 5-field payee (unchanged)", r.partyName.iloc[0], "Ravi Kumar")

# ---- Case 5: HDFC offsetting credit right after matching debit -> REVERSAL ----
t = frame([
    {"description": "NEFT 000123456789 ACME CORP", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 9999,
     "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 100},
    {"description": "NEFT 000123456789 ACME CORP", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 9999,
     "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 10099},
])
r = categorize_HDFC_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("5 HDFC offsetting credit after debit", r.transactionCategory.iloc[1], "REVERSAL")

# regression: a non-transfer offsetting credit (no IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS) stays a bounce
t = frame([
    {"description": "PROPRIETARY COLLECTION 998877", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 500,
     "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 100},
    {"description": "PROPRIETARY COLLECTION 998877", "type": "CREDIT", "amount": 500,
     "remark": "", "balanceAfterTransaction": 600},
])
r = categorize_HDFC_transactions(t, "SAVING")
check("5r HDFC non-transfer offsetting credit (unchanged)", r.transactionCategory.iloc[1], "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE")

print()
print("FAILURES:", failures if failures else "none")
raise SystemExit(1 if failures else 0)

steps.message:
All five complaints traced to exact rules and fixed. As the maintainer predicted, every fault was a boundary or structural offset inside an otherwise-correct rule.

## Fixes

**1. Cheque deposit with all-numeric reference → generic transfer** (mango_saver) — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`
The rule required `remark` length exactly **15** while its own pattern `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 characters — a contradiction that made the rule dead. HDFC reference numbers are 16 chars wide (see the sibling rules `^N[0-9]{15}$` and `^[0-9]{16}$` at HDFC.py:214-215). Fixed `.eq(15)` → `.eq(16)`.

**2. Bare-numeric salary credit lost its SALARY sub-tag** (mango_saver) — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`
The rule compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the account type everywhere in the service (Controller, Purpose, InternalPayment, other banks) is `"SAVING"` — so the condition never fired. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

**3. Leading direction-word narration → empty/wrong counterparty** (rk_ontheroad) — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`
`py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 1 — the direction word ("To"/"From", later blanked by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleaner) — instead of group 2, the name. Fixed `index=0` → `index=1`, matching the identical construction at ICICI.py:168.

**4. Slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer lifting the numeric ref** (auditlens) — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`
For `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>` (exactly 4 fields), the rule took field index 2 (the numeric reference) instead of index 3 (the payee). Fixed `sep_by_(...,2,3)` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`, consistent with the 5-field rule below it which takes the final field.

**5. Offsetting credit after matching debit → bounce instead of reversal** (maintainer) — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`
The reversal rule compared the credit's description against the row **two** back (`shift(periods=2)`) while all other conditions used `shift(periods=1)`, so it never matched an immediately-following credit and fell through to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule. Fixed to `shift(periods=1)`, matching the same rule in ICICI.py:49 and Saraswat.py:20.

## Verification

- A repro script exercising all five synthetic rows: all failed before, all pass after (including guards that 5-field BIL/INFT rows and non-transfer offsetting credits are unchanged).
- A 43-row regression sweep of ordinary HDFC/ICICI narrations diffed against the pre-fix code: **only** the target edge rows changed; every other row is byte-identical.
- Confirmed the restored SALARY sub-tag survives the downstream `purpose()`/`clean_names()` stages (they default-preserve prior values).
